visualPolicy.bannedStyleDescription: Do not use flat beige/green THC-C### course-card infographic posters with dark green title strip, small boxed diagram panels, tiny academic labels, simple flat plant icons, or blank rounded image containers. This style is rejected sitewide and must not be used in product cards, seed cards, education cards, galleries, or Atlas pages.
visualPolicy.replacementRule: Use approved strain/product visuals in seed areas. Use redesigned high-quality Atlas visuals in education areas. If a redesigned visual is not available, leave the image slot empty with a clean non-image placeholder rather than using the banned style.

gaps.title: Flower Anatomy & Reproductive Structures — redesigned visual
gaps.neededVisual: A redesigned high-quality Atlas visual, not the old THC-C course-card poster style. Use cleaner modern educational layout, larger labels, realistic/academic cannabis morphology, and no dark green THC-C header card system.

gaps.title: Trichomes & Secretory Biology — redesigned visual
gaps.neededVisual: A redesigned high-quality Atlas visual, not the old THC-C course-card poster style. Use polished microscopy/reference layout, readable labels, and modern Atlas visual language.

gaps.title: Seed Viability vs Vigor
gaps.neededVisual: A dedicated comparison showing viable versus vigorous lots, final germination percentage, germination speed, uniformity and normal-seedling scoring.

gaps.title: Imbibition → Radicle → Emergence → Establishment
gaps.neededVisual: A dedicated stage sequence separating hydration, radicle protrusion, shoot emergence and normal seedling establishment, with water-temperature-oxygen constraints.

gaps.title: Lifecycle Traceability Record
gaps.neededVisual: A visual record chain linking seed lot or mother ID to propagation date, stage gates, interventions, environmental records and final outcome.

gaps.title: Senescence & Nutrient Remobilization
gaps.neededVisual: A dedicated diagram separating regulated late-stage chlorophyll loss and nutrient remobilization from stress-driven decline.
